environmentalTriggers.message: Potential carbon monoxide hazard! Do not operate an internal combustion engine in an enclosed space without proper ventilation.
Exhaust fumes contain carbon monoxide. Ensure adequate ventilation when working near a running engine.
Airbags contain chemicals that can cause irritation. There is also a risk of secondary deployment. Do not touch or attempt to repair deployed airbags.
A warning light after a collision could indicate a compromised airbag system. Exercise extreme caution as an airbag may deploy unexpectedly.
Brake failure is a critical safety issue. Do not drive the vehicle. Seek immediate professional assistance.
A brake pedal going to the floor indicates a loss of hydraulic pressure. Do not drive the vehicle. This is a severe safety hazard.
Coolant is toxic. Avoid skin contact and ingestion. Leaks can also indicate an overheating engine.
An overheating engine with low coolant suggests a leak or system failure. Do not open a hot radiator cap. Allow the engine to cool completely.
Battery acid is highly corrosive. Avoid contact with skin and eyes. Wear appropriate PPE. Neutralize spills with baking soda.
White powder on battery terminals is typically corrosion from battery acid. Handle with care and wear eye protection.
A vehicle that has fallen off a jack or lift is extremely dangerous. Do not approach or work under an unstable vehicle. Seek professional help.
An unstable vehicle on jacks can fall. Ensure the vehicle is properly secured and on level ground with appropriate jack stands before working underneath.
A fuel leak creates an immediate fire hazard. Avoid any ignition sources. Do not start the engine. Ensure adequate ventilation.
The smell of gasoline or fuel indicates a potential leak and fire risk. Investigate immediately with caution, avoiding sparks or open flames.

environmentalTriggers.pattern: \b(smoke|fire|flames|burning smell|smells like burning|burning wires|aroma of burning)\b
environmentalTriggers.message: Smoke or fire indicates an extreme hazard. Evacuate immediately and call emergency services. Do not attempt to extinguish if unsafe.
Visible flames mean an active fire. Prioritize safety, evacuate all occupants, and call emergency services immediately.

environmentalTriggers.pattern: \b(sparking|electrical fire|burnt wire smell|melting wires|fuses blowing repeatedly)\b
environmentalTriggers.message: Sparking or a burnt wire smell indicates an electrical short circuit, which is a fire hazard. Disconnect the battery if safe to do so.
A short circuit can cause overheating and fire. Do not continue to operate the vehicle. Investigate with caution after disconnecting power.
Refrigerant can cause frostbite or chemical burns. Work in a well-ventilated area and avoid contact with skin and eyes.
A white cloud from the AC system can be refrigerant escaping under pressure. This is a chemical hazard. Do not inhale.

interactionHazards.nounPattern: \b(orange cable|HV battery|high voltage|electric motor cable|inverter cable)\b
interactionHazards.message: High voltage components can cause severe injury or death. Do NOT touch or interact with these components without proper training and safety equipment.
Hybrid and Electric Vehicles contain high voltage systems. Always follow manufacturer's safety procedures before servicing.
Cooling fans can activate unexpectedly, even when the engine is off. Keep hands and tools clear to prevent injury.
Belts and pulleys can cause severe injury if caught while the engine is running. Never work near rotating parts with the engine on.
Pulleys are rotating hazards. Keep clear while the engine is operating.
These components become extremely hot and can cause severe burns. Allow the engine to cool completely before touching.
Never open a radiator cap on a hot engine. Pressurized hot coolant can erupt and cause severe burns.
Engine and exhaust components remain hot for a long time after operation. Risk of severe burns.
AC systems are under high pressure. Refrigerant can cause frostbite or chemical burns. Do not disconnect without proper tools and training.
Fuel systems are pressurized. Releasing pressure improperly can cause fuel to spray, creating a fire hazard and chemical exposure risk.
Brake and power steering lines contain pressurized fluids. Improper handling can lead to fluid leaks and system failure.
Airbag modules contain explosives. Improper handling can lead to accidental deployment, causing severe injury. Always follow safety protocols.
Yellow connectors typically indicate airbag (SRS) system wiring. These are safety-critical components. Do not disconnect or tamper with them without proper safety procedures.

interactionHazards.nounPattern: \b(jacked vehicle|vehicle on jack|car on stands|raised car)\b
interactionHazards.message: Working under a vehicle on a jack alone is dangerous. Always use sturdy jack stands on level ground, or a professional lift.

interactionHazards.nounPattern: \b(under the car|under the vehicle|beneath the car|beneath the vehicle)\b
interactionHazards.message: Do not go under a vehicle unless it is properly supported by jack stands or a certified lift. A jack alone is not sufficient for support.
